note: He is the ICP's flagship occupation and fails almost everything else, which makes him the single most useful data point in this batch for testing the definition. The stated criteria name "a physician, something along those lines" — he is a practising dentist with a parallel career as a touring comedian, so successful is a clean match, and health is unambiguously the neglected area rather than a crisis. But income fails outright: "I definitely don't have 10k to spend, man. Like, it's not even there", no savings, "we're just starting our lives right now", and even three payments of $2,000 were declined. Good-to-great fails in the other direction: at 108-109 kg wanting to lose 15, self-rated 6-7 out of 10 on stiffness, an active knee injury and the words "I've never gotten into the best shape my whole life", this is rescue rather than optimisation. And he trips the exclusion on attitude if not quite on pounds — "in my whole life, I've never trained" and "going to the gym and lifting weights... never appealed to me." The finding for the principal is that professional status and disposable income are being treated as one criterion when they are two, and they come apart badly in the 30-35 bracket, in a weak currency, early in a career.
